nodes.summary: For a natural number $i$ and a list of natural numbers $a_0, \dots, a_{k-1}$, this is the integer $\sum_{j=0}^{k-1} a_j\,(a_j - 2(i + j) - 1)$; the empty list gives $0$.
nodes.title: Shifted row-length sum

nodes.summary: For a partition $\lambda$ of $n$ with row lengths $\lambda_0 \ge \lambda_1 \ge \dots \ge \lambda_{k-1}$, this is the integer $\sum_{i=0}^{k-1} \lambda_i\,(\lambda_i - 2i - 1)$.
nodes.title: Twice the content sum of a partition

nodes.title: Fang–Xia: tilings by transpositions and λ-transitivity

nodes.summary: Let $\lambda$ be a partition of $n$ with row lengths $\lambda_0 \ge \dots \ge \lambda_{k-1}$. A set $Y$ of permutations of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is $\lambda$-transitive, in the sense of Martin and Sagan, if there is a positive integer $r$ such that for any two ordered set partitions $P = (P_0, \dots, P_{k-1})$ and $Q = (Q_0, \dots, Q_{k-1})$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ of shape $\lambda$, exactly $r$ permutations…
nodes.title: λ-transitive sets of permutations

nodes.summary: For subsets $X$ and $Y$ of a group $G$, the pair $(X, Y)$ is a tiling (or factorisation) of $G$ if every $g \in G$ can be written as $g = xy$ with $x \in X$ and $y \in Y$ for exactly one pair $(x, y)$.
nodes.title: Tiling of a group by two subsets

nodes.summary: Let $\lambda$ be a partition of $n$ with row lengths $\lambda_0 \ge \dots \ge \lambda_{k-1}$. An ordered set partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ of shape $\lambda$ is a sequence $(B_0, \dots, B_{k-1})$ of pairwise disjoint subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ whose union is $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and with $|B_i| = \lambda_i$ for every $i$.
nodes.title: Ordered set partition of shape λ

nodes.summary: A partition of $n$ is encoded as a list $(\lambda_0, \lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_{k-1})$ of positive integers with $\lambda_0 \ge \lambda_1 \ge \dots \ge \lambda_{k-1}$ and $\lambda_0 + \dots + \lambda_{k-1} = n$; the $\lambda_i$ are its row lengths.
nodes.title: Integer partition as a list of row lengths

nodes.summary: Let $\lambda$ be a partition of $n$ and let $P = (P_0, \dots, P_{k-1})$ and $Q = (Q_0, \dots, Q_{k-1})$ be ordered set partitions of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ of shape $\lambda$. A permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ sends $P$ to $Q$ if $\sigma(P_i) = Q_i$ for every $i$.
nodes.title: Permutation sending one ordered set partition to another

nodes.summary: $T_n$ is the set of permutations of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ consisting of the identity and all transpositions $(i\ j)$ with $i \ne j$.
